page: Microsoft Azure E8_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Ev3 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a bundled 205 GB SSD, and virtualization is managed by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the E8_v3 sits in the lower tier of modern cloud compute options. Single-core performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% category. Multi-core performance is also modest, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 3030.0 and a passmark CPU score of 5746.58, both placing in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only large block speeds of 35.42 GB/sec and write speeds of 21.7 GB/sec, which are categorized in the bottom 25%.

The primary tradeoff of the E8_v3 is its older CPU architecture and lower processing throughput relative to its high memory capacity. While it offers a generous 64.0 GB of RAM and local SSD storage, it is not suited for compute-heavy workloads, as evidenced by its poor single-threaded compression and decompression benchmarks. However, the high memory density makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU processing. Appropriate workloads include relational databases, caching layers like Redis, and general memory-intensive enterprise applications.
